Transportation Networks, Short-term Mobility, and Pollution Exposure: Evidence from High-Speed Rail in China
abstract: Can the enhanced mobility created by transportation infrastructure investments help people to avoid environmental extremes? We use transaction records from China’s card payment system to measure experienced pollution exposure (EPE)—that is, exposure based on the pollution levels at travelers’ actual locations—and evaluate how EPE was affected by the country’s high-speed railway network, even while holding pollution itself constant. Our estimates imply a reduction in EPE that corresponds to a mortality benefit of 21.3 million life-years saved, primarily due to travelers changing their destinations towards locations with predictably cleaner air.
abstract_zh: 交通基础设施投资所带来的更高流动性，能否帮助人们规避环境极端情况？我们利用中国银行卡支付系统的交易记录，衡量实际经历的污染暴露（EPE），即基于旅行者实际所在地污染水平的暴露程度，并在保持污染本身不变的情况下，评估全国高铁网络如何影响EPE。我们的估计表明，EPE的减少相当于挽救了2130万个生命年的死亡率收益，这主要是由于旅行者将目的地转向空气可预见性更清洁的地区。

Impact of high-speed rail on road traffic and greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Carbon emission reduction in the transportation sector is essential in the global mitigation effort and a large-scale public transport system has the potential to be an effective instrument. High speed rail (HSR) is one such example, yet it is unclear how much reduction in road traffic results from new rail routes. Using the difference-in-differences (DID) method, we show that new HSR routes in China leads to a 20.5 log-point reduction in the number of passenger vehicles and a 15.7 log-point reduction in freight vehicles running on parallel highways. These reductions were not seen on ordinary national roads. These effects translate into an annual reduction of 14.76 million tons of CO2 equivalent of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, or 1.75% of GHG emissions in China’s transport sector. This mitigation effect mainly comes from the substitution of highway goods transport with the conventional railway, instead of the direct replacement of highway passenger transport with HSR. The environmental benefit of HSR in China has not been fully realized because of the thermal-dominated electricity supply. Our further projections suggest that in greener electricity conditions, the HSR in China can significantly contribute more to the reduction in GHG emissions from the transport sector.
abstract_zh: 交通运输部门的碳减排对全球减缓气候变化至关重要，大规模公共交通系统有可能成为有效手段。高速铁路（HSR）即是一例，但新铁路线究竟能在多大程度上减少道路交通，尚不明确。采用双重差分（DID）方法，我们发现中国新开通的高铁线路使平行高速公路上的客运车辆数减少20.5个对数点，货运车辆数减少15.7个对数点。普通国道上未出现这些下降。这些效应相当于每年减少1,476万吨二氧化碳当量的温室气体（GHG）排放，占中国交通部门温室气体排放的1.75%。这一减排效应主要来自公路货运向传统铁路的转移，而非高铁对公路客运的直接替代。由于中国电力供应以火电为主，高铁的环境效益尚未得到充分实现。我们的进一步预测表明，在电力结构更加清洁的情况下，中国高铁可以为交通部门温室气体减排作出显著更大的贡献。
